content:
The test image shows late-season soybean pods that are brown, shriveled, and dried — no white mold, no pustules, no leaf lesions visible. The pods appear poorly developed and desiccated. 

The Diaporthe reference shows stem lesions on a green plant, which doesn't match. Given the shriveled, brown, dull pods at late maturity, **Phomopsis** is the best match — it specifically causes cracked, shriveled, dull seeds and pod blight at late season (R6-R8 growth stages).
